# `sesam help` opens the built-in manual; with a command it shows that
# command's help. Without a terminal the manual falls back to plain markdown on
# stdout.

env PAGER=
env MANPAGER=

# The command overview is still there via --help.
exec sesam --help
stdout 'USAGE:'
! stdout '# FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS'

# A command name shows that command's help.
exec sesam help init
stdout 'sesam init - Initialize sesam in the current repository'
! stdout '# FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS'

# Aliases resolve to their command as well.
exec sesam help s
stdout 'sesam status -'

# Bare help opens the whole manual.
exec sesam help
stdout '# NAME'
stdout '# DESCRIPTION'
stdout '# COMMANDS'
stdout '# FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS'
stdout '# SEE ALSO'
cp stdout embedded.md

# Everything below needs the doc generator, which only a build tagged "docgen"
# carries. `task test` passes the tag; a plain `go test ./...` does not.
[!docgen] stop

# The embedded manual must match what the generator produces right now, or the
# committed docs/manual.md and docs/sesam.1 are stale - run `task docgen`.
exec sesam docgen man --format=markdown --handbook $HANDBOOK
cmp stdout embedded.md

# The man page generator produces roff.
exec sesam docgen man --handbook $HANDBOOK
stdout '^\.TH sesam 1 '
stdout '\.SH FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS'
stdout '\.SH GIT INTEGRATION'

# Subcommands are spelled out in full: roff has no third heading level, so
# "pre-commit" alone would read as a top-level command.
stdout '\.SS hook pre-commit'
stdout '\.SS user add-recipient, ar'

# Environment variables of a flag are part of the generated CLI reference.
exec sesam docgen cli
stdout '--identity, -i.*\\\[\$SESAM_ID, \$SESAM_IDENTITY\\\]'
